items.title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
items.claim: Defines cache storage, freshness, reuse, stale response rules, validation, and Cache-Control directives including max-age, no-cache, no-store, private, public, and s-maxage.

items.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
items.claim: Defines validators, conditional request precedence, and the no-body meaning of 304 Not Modified.

items.title: RFC 5861: HTTP stale controls
items.claim: Defines bounded stale-while-revalidate and stale-if-error permissions; support is not universal.

items.title: RFC 9211: The Cache-Status HTTP Response Header Field
items.claim: Defines optional Cache-Status evidence such as hit and forwarding reasons; absence is not proof of no cache.

items.title: MDN: HTTP caching
items.claim: Provides developer-facing examples for cache states, validators, private/shared caches, and history/bfcache limits.

items.title: MDN: Cache-Control
items.claim: Summarizes directive meanings and compatibility caveats for developer use.

items.title: MDN: Conditional requests
items.claim: Explains ETag and Last-Modified validators, conditional requests, and the fresh-versus-stale lifecycle; notes ETag precedence when both request conditions are present.

items.title: Chrome DevTools Network reference
items.claim: Documents Network inspection, Disable cache, Clear browser cache, replay, and network-condition controls; these change the experiment.

items.title: RFC 9111 §3.5: Cache Handling of Authentication Information
items.claim: A shared cache must not reuse a response to a request containing Authorization unless the response explicitly permits shared reuse with public, s-maxage, or must-revalidate; this protocol rule does not make a user-specific representation safe to share.

items.title: RFC 9110 §§13.1.3 and 13.2.2: Conditional request precedence
items.claim: If-None-Match is evaluated before If-Modified-Since; the date condition is ignored when If-None-Match is present, including when the ETag does not match.

items.title: MDN: ETag
items.claim: Describes ETag as a representation validator used with If-None-Match and the developer trade-off between strong and weak validation.

items.title: MDN: Last-Modified
items.claim: Describes Last-Modified as a date validator used with If-Modified-Since and explains its lower precision compared with ETag in some cases.

items.title: RFC 9111 §2: Overview of Cache Operation
items.claim: Defines the minimum cache-selection information as request method plus target URI and allows additional cache-key material, including Vary-nominated fields or implementation-specific inputs.

items.title: RFC 9111 §4.1: Calculating Cache Response
items.claim: A stored response must not be used without revalidation unless the request fields nominated by Vary match the values in the request that selected the stored response; Vary: * fails ordinary matching.

items.title: RFC 9111 §7.3: Caching of Sensitive Information
items.claim: Set-Cookie alone does not inhibit caching of an otherwise cacheable response; explicit storage policy is needed for sensitive content.

items.title: RFC 9110 §7.1: Determining the Target Resource
items.claim: The target URI excludes only a fragment; path and optional query identify the target resource for the minimum URI comparison.

items.title: RFC 9110 §12.5.5: Vary
items.claim: Describes Vary as the response declaration of request fields that might have influenced representation selection, including the special wildcard.

items.title: RFC 9110 §11.6.2: Authorization
items.claim: Defines Authorization as credentials used by a user agent to authenticate to an origin.

items.title: RFC 6265 §4.2: Cookie
items.claim: Defines the Cookie request field as the user agent serialization of applicable stored cookies; cookie state semantics do not define an HTTP cache key.

items.title: RFC 9111 §3.5: Cache Handling of Authentication Information
items.claim: A shared cache must not reuse a response to a request containing Authorization unless the response explicitly permits shared reuse with public, s-maxage, or must-revalidate; this is not a representation-safety guarantee.

items.title: RFC 9211 §2: Cache-Status
items.claim: Defines optional Cache-Status diagnostics such as hit and forwarding reasons; a field may be omitted and evidence is scoped to the named cache.

items.title: MDN: Vary
items.claim: Provides browser-facing guidance on distinguishing cached responses by nominated request headers and using consistent Vary values.

items.title: MDN: Cookie
items.claim: Describes the optional Cookie request header and its relationship to stored cookie state; it is not presented as a complete cache privacy control.

items.title: MDN: Set-Cookie
items.claim: Provides developer-facing guidance for the response cookie-setting field, distinct from Cache-Control storage policy.

items.title: MDN: Authorization
items.claim: Describes Authorization as credential-bearing request metadata and cross-checks explicit shared-cache permissions.

items.title: RFC 9111 §6: Relationship to Applications
items.claim: Separates HTTP cache requirements from browser history and other application caching mechanisms; a history restoration is not automatically HTTP-cache reuse.

items.title: RFC 9111 §5.1: Age
items.claim: A stored response reused without validation must generate Age, but absence of Age does not imply that the origin was contacted.

items.title: RFC 9110 §7.6.3: Via
items.claim: Via identifies intermediaries that forwarded a message; it is not a cache-hit field.

items.title: Fetch Standard: HTTP header layer division
items.claim: Distinguishes API, service-worker, and network/cache layers; a worker delegation does not by itself identify the downstream response source.

items.title: Fetch Standard: HTTP-network-or-cache fetch
items.claim: Defines the downstream network/cache fetch path that still requires inspection after a service worker delegates.

items.title: Service Workers: Handle Fetch
items.claim: Defines service-worker fetch handling, including the possibility of a worker supplying or delegating a response.

items.title: Service Workers: Caches
items.claim: Named Cache objects are script-managed and origin-associated, separate from the browser HTTP cache.

items.title: HTML: Reloading and traversing
items.claim: Defines session-history traversal and reload as distinct navigation observations for controlled lifecycle tests.

items.title: HTML: Persisted history entry state
items.claim: Provides the persisted-history state boundary used to distinguish a restored document from a newly fetched navigation.

items.title: HTML: PageTransitionEvent
items.claim: Provides the page lifecycle signal used by a test-only pageshow/pagehide log; the signal identifies lifecycle handling, not original response provenance.

items.title: HTML: Document lifecycle and bfcache
items.claim: Documents persisted document lifecycle behavior relevant to back/forward cache diagnosis.

items.title: Chrome DevTools Network panel
items.claim: Provides browser-specific request rows and request metadata for comparing normal, fresh-profile, reload, and disabled-cache conditions.

items.title: Chrome DevTools Network features reference
items.claim: Documents Disable cache, Clear browser cache, service-worker timing phases, and related controls; these change the experiment.

items.title: Chrome DevTools Application panel
items.claim: Provides Chrome-specific inspection for service workers, Cache Storage, storage, and bfcache tools.

items.title: Chrome DevTools bfcache test
items.claim: Cross-checks that bfcache is distinct from browser/HTTP cache and provides a browser-specific test surface.

items.title: RFC 9111 §5.2.2.10: s-maxage
items.claim: For a shared cache, s-maxage overrides max-age and Expires when determining freshness.

items.title: RFC 9111 §5.3: Expires
items.claim: Expires supplies an expiration time when a stronger Cache-Control freshness directive is not present; a past value means stale, not a purge.

items.title: RFC 9111 §5.2.2: Cache-Control
items.claim: Defines the normative meanings of no-cache, no-store, private, max-age, and shared-cache directives used in the CloudFront comparison.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Manage how long content stays in a cache
items.claim: CloudFront expiration behavior uses origin freshness signals with configured minimum/default/maximum TTL bounds and documents the positive-MinTTL override for no-cache, no-store, and private responses.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Cache policies
items.claim: A cache policy attached to a cache behavior defines cache-key inputs and minimum/default/maximum TTL settings; an all-zero policy disables caching and a positive minimum can override origin directives.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront API: CachePolicyConfig
items.claim: The cache policy configuration contains default, minimum, and maximum TTL values and documents the warning that a positive minimum can cause caching despite no-cache, no-store, or private.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront API: CacheBehavior
items.claim: A cache behavior uses CachePolicyId or legacy ForwardedValues; legacy TTL fields are deprecated and the matching behavior must be identified before interpreting a response.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Response headers policies
items.claim: A Cache-Control value added or overridden for the viewer controls browser caching and does not change how CloudFront caches the object; Server-Timing can expose sampled CloudFront metrics when enabled.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Invalidate files
items.claim: Invalidation removes selected objects from CloudFront edge caches, while versioned filenames avoid waiting for old objects; neither is a universal purge of local or downstream caches.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Specify files for invalidation
items.claim: Invalidation paths are distribution-relative and case-sensitive; trailing wildcards, query strings, variants, rewrites, and slash forms affect scope.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Invalidation requests
items.claim: An invalidation request has an identifier and status; operators can inspect the request and wait for Completed, which describes CloudFront operation status.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Update existing objects
items.claim: AWS recommends version identifiers for frequently updated files and documents their deployment and rollback trade-offs relative to invalidation.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Invalidation pricing
items.claim: The current pricing documentation states the monthly free path allowance and billing treatment for invalidation paths and wildcards.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Quotas
items.claim: The current quota documentation states invalidation path/tag and wildcard request-rate limits used in the report.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront API: CreateInvalidation
items.claim: CreateInvalidation accepts a path-based invalidation request and returns an invalidation identifier for tracking.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront API: GetInvalidation
items.claim: GetInvalidation exposes the status and details of a named invalidation so an operator can verify completion.

items.title: RFC 9111 §5.2.2.10: s-maxage
items.claim: For a shared cache, s-maxage overrides max-age and Expires; max-age is not required for the shared-cache lifetime.

items.title: RFC 9111 §4.2.1: calculating freshness
items.claim: Defines explicit freshness precedence and the boundary between freshness semantics and a measured product result.

items.title: RFC 9111 §5.3: Expires
items.claim: An Expires date supplies freshness when stronger directives do not apply; expiration is not a purge command.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Manage how long content stays in a cache
items.claim: CloudFront documents max-age or s-maxage as origin TTL inputs, privacy behavior, and the positive-MinTTL override; its detailed table does not provide a standalone s-maxage-only worked row.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Understand cache policies
items.claim: The selected cache policy supplies cache-key inputs and MinTTL/DefaultTTL/MaxTTL; the attached behavior must be inspected instead of assumed.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront API: CachePolicyConfig
items.claim: MinTTL is required; the API documents default values and the explicit-header boundary for DefaultTTL and MaxTTL.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront API: CacheBehavior
items.claim: The first matching behavior, CachePolicyId, response-headers policy, and deprecated legacy fields must be read together.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Understand response headers policies
items.claim: A Cache-Control value added or overridden for the viewer does not change how CloudFront caches the object.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Specify files for invalidation
items.claim: Path, query, wildcard, variant, rewrite, and directory-form rules determine invalidation scope; effective cache-key inputs must be inspected.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Invalidation requests
items.claim: An invalidation ID and accepted request are not completion evidence; GetInvalidation status Completed is the named operation’s completion signal.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront API: CreateInvalidation
items.claim: CreateInvalidation returns the request details and identifier for tracking, not proof that the batch finished.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront API: GetInvalidation
items.claim: GetInvalidation exposes the named invalidation status; Completed is the completion evidence used by the audit.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Update existing objects
items.claim: Versioned names create a new cache target and help bypass old local/corporate copies; they do not delete the old URL.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront: Lambda@Edge event structure
items.claim: A viewer-request URI rewrite changes the request path; the audit retains AWS’s explicit two-path invalidation guidance for Lambda@Edge without generalizing it to every stage.

items.title: Amazon CloudFront Functions event structure
items.claim: A changed URI changes the requested object, but the audit does not claim the Lambda@Edge two-path invalidation instruction is universal for Functions.
